We need to extract explicit facts.

Text: "Constitution of India

The Constitution of India (IAST: Bhāratīya Saṃvidhāna) is the supreme law of India. The document lays down the framework demarcating fundamental political code, structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens. It is the longest written constitution of any country on earth. B.R. Ambedkar, chairman of the drafting committee, is widely considered to be its chief architect."

We need triplets.

Entities: Constitution of India (document). Relation: "supreme law of" -> India. So subject: Constitution of India, relation: "supreme law of", object: India. subject_type: "legal document" maybe. object_type: "sovereign state". qualifiers none.

Second sentence: "The document lays down the framework demarcating fundamental political code, structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens."

We need to split into multiple facts. The document (Constitution of India) "lays down" "framework demarcating fundamental political code, structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions". That's a bit complex. Could break into multiple relations: "has component" maybe. But we need explicit statements. It says "lays down the framework demarcating ...". Could capture as relation "framework includes" with object list? Might be too vague. Perhaps we can capture separate facts: "Constitution of India" "demarcates" "fundamental political code". Also "demarcates" "structure". "demarcates" "procedures". "demarcates" "powers". "demarcates" "duties of government institutions". Also "sets out" "fundamental rights". "sets out" "directive principles". "sets out" "duties of citizens". These are explicit.

We need subject_type "legal document". object_type maybe "concept" or "political concept". Use generic "concept". We'll assign.

Third sentence: "It is the longest written constitution of any country on earth." So relation: "length superlative" maybe "longest written constitution". Could be relation "longest written constitution of" with object "any country on earth". But we need subject: Constitution of India, relation: "longest written constitution of", object: "any country on earth". Or maybe relation "longest written constitution" with qualifier "point in time"? Not needed. We'll create relation "longest written constitution of" object "any country on earth". subject_type "legal document". object_type "concept". Could also use "superlative" but okay.

Fourth: "B.R. Ambedkar, chairman of the drafting committee, is widely considered to be its chief architect."

We have B.R. Ambedkar as subject. Relation: "position held" maybe "chairman of" object "drafting committee". Also "chief architect of" object "Constitution of India". The phrase "is widely considered to be its chief architect" indicates attribution and modality? It's an attribution (widely considered) and maybe modality "considered". Should we add qualifier "attribution" with object "widely considered"? The rule: preserve modality, attribution. So relation "chief architect of" with qualifier "attribution" "widely considered". Also maybe "polarity" positive. We'll add qualifier "attribution" "widely considered". Also we have "chairman of the drafting committee". That's a factual role. No attribution.

11. B.R. Ambedkar - position held - chairman of drafting committee. (maybe relation "chairman of" object "drafting committee". Use "position held". We'll use relation "chairman of". object "drafting committee". qualifiers [].

12. B.R. Ambedkar - chief architect of - Constitution of India. qualifiers: attribution "widely considered".
